resolution.title: [pytest] Rename 'platform' directory to 'platform_tests' to avoid conflicts
resolution.description:
Rename 'platform' directory to 'platform_tests', because a directory named 'platform' causes conflicts, resulting in the following error when invoking some Ansible modules from pytest:

```
>   raise RunAnsibleModuleFail("run module {} failed, errmsg {}".format(self.module_name, res))
E   RunAnsibleModuleFail: run module wait_for failed, errmsg {'exception': u'Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 114, in <module>
  File "<stdin>", line 106, in _ansiballz_main
  File "<stdin>", line 49, in invoke_module
  File "/tmp/ansible_wait_for_payload_fMRgQL/__main__.py", line 239, in <module>
  File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/psutil/__init__.py", line 50, in <module>
    from ._compat import long
  File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/psutil/_compat.py", line 113, in <module>
    if platform.python_implementation() != "CPython":
AttributeError: 'module' object has no attribute 'python_implementation'
', '_ansible_no_log': False, 'rc': 1, 'msg': u'MODULE FAILURE
See stdout/stderr for the exact error', 'module_stderr': u'Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 114, in <module>
  File "<stdin>", line 106, in _ansiballz_main
  File "<stdin>", line 49, in invoke_module
  File "/tmp/ansible_wait_for_payload_fMRgQL/__main__.py", line 239, in <module>
  File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/psutil/__init__.py", line 50, in <module>
    from ._compat import long
  File "/usr/local/lib/python2.7/dist-packages/psutil/_compat.py", line 113, in <module>
    if platform.python_implementation() != "CPython":
AttributeError: 'module' object has no attribute 'python_implementation'
', 'changed': False, 'module_stdout': u''}
```

This is because some modules (in this example, psutil, via the 'wait_for' Ansible module) are looking for `platform.python_implementation()` to determine Python compatibility, and since we have a local directory named 'platform', this is the directory it checks. I also found someone else who had a similar issue here: https://github.com/psf/requests/issues/2376#issuecomment-66581919

Per @wangxin, this PR also resolves https://github.com/Azure/sonic-mgmt/issues/1659
